claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi matrix is single-phase and homogeneous in its as-processed state.
An ultrathin coating of 2D HEA nanoflakes can act as a tribo-reactive coating on CoCrFeNi.
Sliding of the coated CoCrFeNi surface will induce in-situ formation of an adaptive oxide layer.
The sliding-induced oxide layer will be continuous and lubricious.
At lower temperatures, the 2D HEA nanoflake coating will provide boundary lubrication.
As temperature increases, the coating's catalytic activity will trigger controlled oxidation.
The resulting oxide will form a stable, low-shear film.
The oxide film will continuously accommodate changes in load and environmental conditions.
The proposed coating-and-oxide mechanism will prevent excessive friction and wear.
Relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi, coated CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
The tribological improvement will be more pronounced at high temperatures because of effective in-situ oxide formation.
The intervention will remain effective over applied loads from 1 to 9 N.
The intervention will remain effective in ambient, oxygen-containing atmospheres.
The intervention will remain effective in inert atmospheres.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may depend on coating uniformity, coating thickness, and environmental oxygen level.

contradictions.description: The proposed high-temperature mechanism requires controlled oxidation and is stated to depend on oxygen, yet the intervention is also expected to work in inert atmospheres without identifying an alternative oxygen source or an oxidation-independent high-temperature mechanism.
